description: issue #681 (slice I2), the NUMBER half of the number-vs-word rule: `spec/interaction-events.md:136-137` — "If the submitted text parses as an OpenLogo number literal, the reporter returns a number." The scripted answer is the TEXT "42" (the raw characters a learner would type) and the read reports the NUMBER 42. Both recorded assertions DISCRIMINATE number from word: the `print` payload records the JSON number `42`, not the string `"42"`, and `:answer is a "number"` reports `true`, which the word "42" would not (`spec/grammar.md:230`: `is a` accepts any value). Note that arithmetic would NOT discriminate here — OpenLogo's `+` coerces a numeric word, so `:answer + 1` reports 43 whether the read returned the number 42 or the word "42"; a fixture built on it would look like proof of this branch while being inert against an implementation that never reports numbers at all. Pair with `input-word-answer`, which scripts a non-numeral through the same shape and records `false` for the identical `is a "number"` question. Per the maintainer's #657 ruling `input` is tested by MOCKING the answer through `executeOptions.hostInput.responses` (a FIFO consumed in order by each `input` call), and the read introduces NO new event kind: it emits the ordinary catch-all `primitive` event named `input` (`spec/interaction-events.md:105-106`) AFTER the read finishes, so `spec/execution-model.md`'s trace/event registry is unchanged. The payload carries only `name` — never the prompt or the submitted text — and no `turtle_id`, because a read concerns no turtle.
